walkthroughs.body_html:
Independent Investigation (NEA) — a core area of A-Level Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Independent Investigation (NEA) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Independent Investigation (NEA).

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What was the Tohoku earthquake magnitude?
What changed between the MDGs (Millennium Development Goals) and the SDGs (Sustainable Development Goals)?
options: MDGs and SDGs are the same — just renamed.
The SDGs replaced the MDGs because the MDGs were achieved.
All earthquakes of magnitude 7 cause the same damage everywhere.
MDGs (2000-2015) targeted LICs on basic poverty/health/education; SDGs (2015-2030) apply to all countries and include environmental and inequality goals — broader, more universal scope.

mcqs.q: Why do earthquakes of similar magnitude cause different amounts of damage?
options: Damage depends on depth, distance from population, building quality, ground type (liquefaction risk), time of day, and emergency preparedness — not just magnitude.
MDGs and SDGs are the same — just renamed.
Bigger magnitude always means more deaths.
All earthquakes of magnitude 7 cause the same damage everywhere.

mcqs.q: What drives the movement of tectonic plates?
options: Convection currents in the mantle combined with slab pull at subduction zones and ridge push at constructive boundaries.
The Earth's rotation makes the plates move.
MDGs and SDGs are the same — just renamed.
Plates move because of ocean tides pulling on the crust.

sequence.def: Set the aim and a testable hypothesis before any fieldwork
Use sampling (random/systematic) to gather data in the field
Organise into tables, graphs and maps (e.g. choropleth)
Apply tests like Spearman's Rank to find relationships
Answer the hypothesis using the evidence gathered
Assess reliability, limitations and how to improve the study
